wait_6m.label: Waited over 6 months for specialised care, per 10 000
wait_6m.title_fi: Erikoissairaanhoitoa yli 6 kk odottaneet vuoden aikana / 10 000 asukasta
wait_6m.title_en: Patients waiting over 6 months during the year for access to specialised health care per 10 000 inhabitants
wait_6m.description_en:
The indicator gives the number of patients waiting over 6 months for access to specialised health care per ten thousand inhabitants in a given year. The indicator is calculated as an average of the data reported monthly by the wellbeing services counties. Population proportions are calculated at THL based on the Population Statistics of Statistics Finland.


A patient is considered to be waiting for treatment when a physician or another health care professional has, based on an assessment of the need for treatment, made a treatment decision and placed the patient on a waiting list for treatment (the reason for queueing is hospital resources) or booked an appointment in outpatient care for the patient. Patients queuing for treatment include patients who are waiting for an operation, procedure or other treatment.


The date of placement in the treatment queue is the date when the patient is placed in the queue for treatment, operation or procedure. The date of placement in the treatment queue should be the same date when the physician has decided on treatment. The extraction includes patients who have a scheduled appointment and patients who do not have a scheduled appointment even when the required treatment has been decided on. The extraction includes patients whose reason for queuing belongs to the category of hospital resources or urgent care, excluding emergency room patients.


The patients waiting for treatment do not include those waiting for treatment to be provided at a specific point in time, such as one year later, due to medical reasons. The patients waiting for treatment also do not include those receiving recurring treatment or monitoring of illness at specific intervals.

wait_median.label: Median wait for specialised care (31 Dec)
wait_median.title_en: Wait time for patients awaiting specialised health care as of 31 December, median
wait_median.description_en:
The indicator represents the median waiting time (the middle value of observations ordered by size) for specialist care in the hospitals of the hospital districts.


A patient is considered to be waiting for treatment when a physician or another health care professional has, based on the assessment of the need for treatment, made a treatment decision and placed the patient in a queue for treatment (the reason for queuing is hospital resources or urgent care). Patients queuing for treatment include patients who are waiting for an operation, procedure or other treatment. In outpatient services, patients queuing for treatment include patients waiting for invasive cardiological examination and treatment, rehabilitation of hearing as well as psychiatric examination and psychotherapy.


The date of placement in the treatment queue is the date when the patient is placed in the queue for treatment, operation or procedure. The date of placement in the treatment queue should be the same date when the physician has decided on treatment. The extraction includes patients who have a scheduled appointment and patients who do not have a scheduled appointment even when the required treatment has been decided on. The extraction includes patients whose reason for queuing belongs to the category of hospital resources or urgent care, excluding emergency room patients. The index gives provider-specific information. The patients waiting for treatment in hospitals in a hospital district are mainly residents of the hospital district in question.

onc_visits.label: Outpatient visits, oncology and radiotherapy
onc_visits.title_en: Outpatient visits in specialised health care, oncology and radiotherapy
onc_visits.description_en:
The indicator gives outpatient visits in oncology and radiotherapy during the year. Oncology and radiotherapy include all outpatient visits in specialised health care within the speciality of oncology and radiotherapy in all municipal hospitals, including specialist-led health-centre hospitals. The numbers do not include day hospital treatment.



In the statistics, outpatient visits in specialised health care are medical consultation visits by clients/patients.

cancer_meds.label: Special refund for cancer medicines, age-standardised
cancer_meds.title_fi: Erityiskorvattaviin lääkkeisiin syövän vuoksi oikeutetut 31.12., ikävakioitu väestöosuus (%)
cancer_meds.title_en: Entitled to special refunds on medicines for cancer 31.12., age-standardised population share(%)
cancer_meds.description_en:
The indicator shows the age-standardised percentage (%) of population living in Finland who were entitled to at least one of the following refunds: 115 Breast cancer, 116 Prostate cancer, 117 Leukaemia and other malignant diseases of the blood and bone marrow, and malignant diseases of the lymphatic tissue, 128 Cancers of female genital organs, 130 Malignant tumour, 180 Interferon alfa.

Detailed definition: Excluding persons entitled to compensation based on diagnosis D721.1 or any diagnosis starting with D75.

The age standardisation was carried out in 5-year age groups, with those aged 85 and over as the highest category. The standard population is the total population of the country in the year in question, with those who lived abroad or whose place of residence was unknown at the end of the year excluded from the total number of cases in the country.

surv_breast.label: 5-year relative survival, breast cancer
surv_breast.title_fi: Rintasyövän sairastaneiden viiden vuoden suhteellinen elossaololuku, %
surv_breast.title_en: Five-year relative survival rate of breast cancer patients, %
surv_breast.description_en:
The indicator represents the five-year relative age-standardised survival rate of breast cancer patients, (0100 percent). The figure indicates the percentage of cancer patients alive five years after cancer diagnosis, compared to the percentage of the population of a similar age in the region surviving during this time. The relative survival rate can be interpreted as an estimate of the likelihood of survival in a situation where the cancer of the patient is the only possible cause of death.
This is based on the monitoring of patients diagnosed during the statistical year visible on Sotkanet, and during the nine preceding years, carried out during the statistical year and the four years preceding the statistical year. The regional survival rates have been age-standardised to correspond to the age structure of the patients diagnosed in the entire country during the monitoring years.

population.label: Population at year end
population.description_en: The indicator gives the permanent resident population (males and females combined) of a municipality on the last day of the year. Those who according to the Population Information System are domiciled in Finland at the end of the year belong to the permanent resident population whatever their nationality, as do Finnish nationals temporarily residing abroad.

age65_share.label: Population aged 65+, % of total
age65_share.title_en: Population aged 65 and over as % of total population
age65_share.description_en:
The indicator gives the permanent resident population in the age group as a percentage of the total permanent resident population by gender (males and females separately and combined) on the last day of the year.

Population proportions are calculated at THL based on the Population Statistics of Statistics Finland.

foreign_lang.label: Native language other than Finnish, Swedish or Sami, per 1000
foreign_lang.title_fi: Muu kuin suomi, ruotsi tai saame äidinkielenä / 1 000 asukasta
foreign_lang.title_en: Native language other than Finnish, Swedish or Sami per 1000 inhabitants
foreign_lang.description_en:
The indicator gives the number of people with a native language other than the official languages of Finland (Finnish, Swedish and Sami) per thousand inhabitants. The group of people with a native language other than the official languages also includes cases where the language is unknown.

Population refers to the permanent resident population of the municipality. Those who according to the Population Information System were domiciled in Finland on 31 December 2003 are included in the population whatever their nationality, as well as Finnish citizens and foreign nationals temporarily residing abroad. Foreign nationals are domiciled in Finland if their stay is intended to last or has lasted at least twelve months. An asylum-seeker will not be granted a legal domicile until his/her application has been approved. Persons attached to foreign embassies, trade missions and consulates, as well as their family members and personal staff, are not counted among the resident population unless they are Finnish citizens. On the contrary, the Finnish staff of Finland's embassies and trade missions abroad and persons serving in the UN peacekeeping forces are counted among the resident population.

Population proportions are calculated at THL based on the Population Statistics of Statistics Finland.

edu_level.label: Measure of educational level
edu_level.description_en:
The indicator gives the level of education in the population, giving the average length of education and training required for each person's highest educational qualification or degree after basic education.

The measure of educational level describes the educational level of a population group by length of education per person. For example, the value 246 shows that the theoretical length of education per person is 2.5 years after completing basic education. The measure usually covers the population aged 20 and over because most under-20s are still in school, so they have not yet been able to attain a qualification or degree.



Population having completed a qualification or degree refers to completers of general upper secondary schools, vocational educational establishments, polytechnics and universities, as well as attainers of initial, further and specialist vocational qualifications through competence tests. Those who have only completed basic education are not included. Qualifications and degrees are classified according to each person's highest, most recent vocational qualification or degree.
